haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine computes into the shadow store only, which holds computed but uncharged invoices.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes into the shadow store only.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared, read from comparison_results. A person runs the rollout tool to move it.
haiku-low.q4: The billing monitor starts a rollback when new-engine charge failure rate exceeds 2% over any 10-minute window. This happens only in both or new_only, not shadow.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Before the new engine can take over again, the rollout must go through shadow again and the 7-day count starts over.
haiku-low.q6: Rollback from new_only is possible within 35 days in new_only. After decommissioning, allowed after 35 days, there is no way back. The document gives no further reason.
haiku-low.q7: Engines read billing_mode at the start of each run and re-read billing_mode and charging_paused before each charge. An invoice mid-process is not charged if the check fails, and is charged on the next run.
haiku-low.q8: Evidence is kept in comparison_results, written by the nightly comparison job. The rollout tool refuses a move if the gate is not met or a rollback is in progress.
haiku-low.q9: The billing monitor measures the new engine's charge failure rate. When it exceeds 2% over any 10-minute window in both or new_only, it calls the rollback runner.
haiku-low.q10: Customers due meanwhile wait. They are charged in the reconcile step, when the old engine charges what is due and not yet charged.
haiku-low.q11: The ledger holds at most one charge per customer and period and rejects a second. Reconcile checks the ledger before charging, and the charge check stops the new engine after switch_to_old.
haiku-low.q12: The rollback record keeps the failed step, and the runner retries it. Each step is safe to repeat. If the runner crashes, the document says NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: The old engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The new engine computes into the shadow store only (not charged).
sonnet.q2: The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes into the shadow store only.
sonnet.q3: 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared, read from comparison_results. A person runs the rollout tool to make the move.
sonnet.q4: The billing monitor starts it automatically when the charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. This applies in both and new_only (not shadow).
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. The gates reset: the rollout must go through shadow again and the 7-day count starts over (then the later gates).
sonnet.q6: After 35 days in new_only. Moving to decommissioned is allowed after 35 days and from then on there is no way back. The document gives no explicit reason for 35 days beyond that matching the usage event log's 35-day retention, which it does not state as the reason.
sonnet.q7: Each engine reads billing_mode at the start of every billing run. Before each charge it re-reads billing_mode and charging_paused (the charge check) and charges only if the mode names it as charging engine and charging is not paused; so a run that started before the change cannot charge after it. A charge missed this way is made on the next billing run.
sonnet.q8: In comparison_results, written by the nightly comparison job. The rollout tool refuses to move forward if the gate is not met (or a rollback is in progress).
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate (above 2% over any 10-minute window, in both or new_only). When met, it calls the rollback runner to start the rollback.
sonnet.q10: Charges due wait while charging_paused is on (neither engine charges). They are made in the reconcile step, by the old engine; after resume_charging the old engine charges normally again.
sonnet.q11: The ledger holds at most one charge per customer and billing period: the engine checks the ledger and skips if one exists, and the ledger rejects a second one. reconcile also checks the ledger before charging.
sonnet.q12: The rollback record keeps the failed step and the runner retries it; each step is safe to repeat because reconcile checks the ledger before charging. The exact billing state at the moment of failure is not described beyond that. What resumes it if the runner itself crashes is not decided (open question), and who alerts if a step keeps failing is also open.
